headline: A research team led by He Kaiming says it has helped Claude Opus 5 clear every public level of the ARC-AGI-3 reasoning test by letting the model see game images and revisit past frames.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 1: preprint results from the authors, reported by one outlet, on the public games only.
importance_line: If it holds up, the result suggests that how a model sees and remembers a task can matter as much as the model itself, but the 100 score comes from the authors' own setup on public games and awaits outside review.
summary: 36Kr reports on a new arXiv paper, VISTA, from He Kaiming's team, saying Claude Opus 5 scored 100 on all 25 public games of ARC-AGI-3, a test of learning unfamiliar interactive games, using about 0.43 times the steps of first-time human players. The team gave the model screenshots instead of a grid of numbers plus a searchable frame history, whereas the same model scored about 40 in the official standard setup; this is the authors' claim, not yet reviewed by others.
notes: Source is the VISTA preprint as relayed by 36Kr; 'He Kaiming's team' per 36Kr.
